question: to the Commission Elena Donazzan (ECR), Carlo Fidanza (ECR), Nicola Procaccini (ECR), Antonella Sberna (ECR), Pietro Fiocchi (ECR), Michele Picaro (ECR), Mariateresa Vivaldini (ECR), Alberico Gambino (ECR), Daniele Polato (ECR), Stefano Cavedagna (ECR) Subject:
Regulation (EU) 2023/2055 for industrial downstream users of plastics: distinction between producers and processors

Regulation (EU) 2023/2055, which amends Annex XVII to REACH, prohibits the placing on the market of synthetic polymer microparticles ‘intentionally present [...] to confer a soughtafter characteristic’ and imposes annual reporting obligations on ECHA. Among the entities obliged to follow that rule, paragraph 11 of the annex includes ‘industrial downstream users’, which also formally includes thermoplastic polymer processors. However, the regulation does not distinguish between entities that produce intentionally added microplastics and those such as processors who buy and process already compliant raw materials without adding any microparticles. In this scenario – where microplastics are not ‘intentionally present [...] to confer a sought-after characteristic’ – it is unclear whether the reporting requirements apply. Neither ECHA nor the national authorities have provided operational guidance, exposing SMEs to the risk of formal non-compliance or to consultancy fees that are disproportionate to their actual responsibility in the dispersion of microplastics. In the light of the above, can the Commission clarify whether the obligations laid down in paragraph 11 of the annex to Regulation (EU) 2023/2055 apply to processing companies that buy raw materials that are already compliant, without intentionally adding microparticles? If they do, with which operational tools other than those designed for chemical producers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.9.2026) Entry 78 of Annex XVII to the Regulation on the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of chemicals (REACH)1 (“the microplastics restriction”) allows synthetic polymer microparticles (“microplastics”) to be placed on the market for industrial use by the derogation under paragraph 4(a). This means that industrial users may buy these microplastics as raw materials for their own production in compliance with the restriction. However, using these derogated microplastics in industrial production triggers the reporting obligation under paragraph 11 of the same entry. In contrast, if the raw material does not contain any microparticles, then the restriction, including the reporting obligations, does not apply. To support implementation of the microplastic restriction, the Commission has published a specific Explanatory Guide2. It explains in simple terms the provisions and the intended implementation of the restriction, including for reporting. In addition, questions on REACH implementation, including the microplastics restriction, can be addressed to the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA)3 or the REACH national helpdesks4. Detailed operational instructions on how to report estimated microplastics emissions to ECHA are published on the ECHA website5.
